decisions.reason: The complete Definition deliberately specifies a Floer package conditional on valid regular data, and fixes the standard absolute-grading normalization and cobordism degree convention; it does not claim to prove existence. This is mathematically consistent. Ozsvath–Szabo math/0110170v1, Section 2, printed pp.7–8, separates relative theory from the absolute-grading existence theorem and gives the same normalization and degree formula. The local lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps supplies that existence separately, and lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance explicitly invokes it. The title does not turn a definition into an existence theorem.

F1 incorrectly attributes a four-dimensional boundary assertion to def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot, whose Definition only constructs the three-dimensional exterior cover and filling. The assertion itself is true and is already supplied by the declared F2 dependency: its Statement and proof 4.1 identify the boundary using the collared normal square map. This is a redundant misattribution, not a missing mathematical premise. Repaired F1 to state only the exterior/filling convention, expanded F2 accurately, and cited F2 in step 2.1, including the boundary-orientation check.
